name: Govern yourself before governing others
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book I — Concerning Discipline
modern_rule: Before acting, check anger, ego, fear and impulse. A leader who cannot regulate himself will misread people and misuse authority.
workplace_use: Do not make disciplinary, staffing or escalation decisions while emotionally activated.
ethical_boundary: Self-control is not emotional suppression; safety or misconduct still requires timely action.

name: Seek experienced counsel
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book I — Concerning Discipline
modern_rule: Use experienced people as an information advantage, while retaining independent judgment.
workplace_use: Before changing a technical process, consult operators, maintenance, quality and engineering where relevant.
ethical_boundary: Expertise is evidence, not infallibility.

name: Protect unfinished deliberations
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book I — counsel and deliberation
modern_rule: Share sensitive plans on a need-to-know basis until they are ready for responsible communication.
workplace_use: Do not casually disclose personnel matters, negotiations, investigations or unapproved plans.
ethical_boundary: Never conceal required safety, legal, quality or compliance information.

name: Deliberate from more than one viewpoint
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book I — counsel and ministers
modern_rule: Important decisions should be stress-tested from operational, human, financial and long-term perspectives.
workplace_use: For a production decision, consider safety, quality, throughput, maintenance and team effects—not only output.
ethical_boundary: Consultation should improve judgment, not be used to diffuse accountability.

name: Know the objective before choosing the means
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Books VI–VII — state elements and policy choices
modern_rule: Separate what you want to achieve from the method you initially prefer.
workplace_use: If the objective is reliable procedure compliance, coaching, redesign, training or discipline are alternative means—not the objective itself.
ethical_boundary: Objectives must remain lawful and ethically defensible.

name: Assess relative strength before confrontation
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Books VI–VII — relative strength and policy
modern_rule: Map formal authority, expertise, relationships, information, alternatives and constraints before taking a hard position.
workplace_use: A title may give formal authority while another person has technical or social influence. Account for both.
ethical_boundary: Power analysis is for better decisions, not exploitation.

name: Timing changes the value of an action
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Books VII–IX — policy, preparation and campaigns
modern_rule: A correct action at the wrong time can still fail. Evaluate readiness, urgency, audience and circumstances.
workplace_use: Correct privately when possible; interrupt immediately when safety, food quality or serious risk demands it.
ethical_boundary: Strategic timing must not become avoidance of necessary action.

name: Reduce uncertainty before committing
classical_basis: Arthashastra — extensive emphasis on intelligence and verification
modern_rule: When uncertainty is high and delay is affordable, gather facts before escalating or committing.
workplace_use: Check trends, records, witnesses and equipment state before assigning blame.
ethical_boundary: Do not investigate intrusively or outside legitimate professional boundaries.

name: Corroborate important information
classical_basis: Arthashastra — intelligence systems and cross-checking
modern_rule: High-impact claims should not depend on one interested source when independent evidence is available.
workplace_use: Verify a process incident using PLC trends, logs, samples, equipment condition and accounts from relevant staff.
ethical_boundary: Use legitimate evidence sources; no covert surveillance or privacy violations.

name: Analyze interests, not only stated positions
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Books VI–VII — alliances and competing interests
modern_rule: Ask what incentives, fears, status needs, constraints or goals may sit underneath a person's stated position.
workplace_use: Resistance to a change may reflect workload, competence concerns, loss of autonomy or genuine technical objections.
ethical_boundary: Treat inferred motives as hypotheses, not facts.

name: Sama — start with reasoned alignment
classical_basis: Classical Indian statecraft; conciliatory/persuasive means used throughout Arthashastra traditions
modern_rule: Use explanation, listening, shared goals and relationship before coercive measures when the risk allows it.
workplace_use: Clarify expectations and the reason behind them before assuming defiance.
ethical_boundary: Persuasion must not become deception.

name: Dana — align incentives
classical_basis: Classical Indian statecraft; inducement/incentive as a strategic means
modern_rule: Make cooperation easier or more worthwhile through recognition, resources, reciprocity, ownership or removal of friction.
workplace_use: Give a skilled operator ownership of improving a standard rather than treating expertise as a threat.
ethical_boundary: Do not use improper inducements, favoritism or conflicts of interest.

name: Bheda — distinguish interests and fault lines
classical_basis: Classical Indian statecraft; differentiation/division as a strategic means
modern_rule: Separate issues, stakeholders and motives so you do not treat a coalition or conflict as one undifferentiated problem.
workplace_use: Determine whether resistance is one person's issue, a training gap, a process-design problem or a wider team norm.
ethical_boundary: In professional life, use this for stakeholder analysis—not rumor, sabotage or malicious division.

name: Danda — use legitimate authority proportionally
classical_basis: Arthashastra — punishment, enforcement and order
modern_rule: When persuasion and correction fail—or risk is serious—use documented, proportionate and legitimate authority.
workplace_use: For repeated deliberate non-compliance, move from coaching to formal accountability through proper policy.
ethical_boundary: No humiliation, retaliation, threats or disproportionate punishment.

name: Asana — sometimes the best move is to hold position
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — neutrality/remaining quiet as one of the six policies
modern_rule: Do not confuse activity with progress. If acting now worsens your position and waiting is safe, preserve options.
workplace_use: Avoid reacting to a minor provocation when facts are incomplete and no immediate operational risk exists.
ethical_boundary: Waiting is unacceptable when people, safety, compliance or serious harm are at risk.

name: Sandhi — cooperate when cooperation improves position
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — peace/agreement
modern_rule: Cooperation can be strategic even when parties do not fully agree.
workplace_use: Build workable agreements between production, maintenance and quality around shared outcomes.
ethical_boundary: Do not make agreements you cannot honor.

name: Vigraha — confront when continued accommodation costs more
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — conflict/war as a policy option
modern_rule: Some conflicts require a clear boundary, disagreement or escalation after softer options are exhausted or urgency is high.
workplace_use: Stop unsafe work even if doing so creates interpersonal conflict.
ethical_boundary: Professional confrontation means clear boundaries and process—not aggression.

name: Yana — prepare before the decisive move
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — marching/preparation as policy
modern_rule: Build evidence, allies, resources and alternatives before a high-stakes move.
workplace_use: Before proposing a major process change, collect data, expected benefits, risks and implementation requirements.
ethical_boundary: Preparation should not become political scheming against people.

name: Build reliable allies before you need them
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VI — allies as an element of power
modern_rule: Trust and cross-functional relationships are strategic assets created through consistent value and reliability.
workplace_use: Maintain good working relationships with operations, maintenance, quality, engineering and management before crises occur.
ethical_boundary: Alliances should not become cliques or exclusion.

name: Resources constrain strategy
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Books II and VI — treasury, resources and state elements
modern_rule: A plan without time, competence, tools, money or capacity is not yet a strategy.
workplace_use: Before committing to output or maintenance work, verify staffing, materials, equipment state and time.
ethical_boundary: Do not demand impossible outcomes and transfer the cost to subordinates.

name: Trust people; design controls anyway
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book II — administration, accounting and misappropriation controls
modern_rule: Good systems reduce dependence on perfect memory or perfect character.
workplace_use: Use logs, verification, reconciliation and clear ownership for critical tasks.
ethical_boundary: Controls should be proportionate and transparent, not a culture of suspicion.

name: Match responsibility with accountability
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book II — duties of superintendents
modern_rule: Assign clear ownership, expectations and verification for important work.
workplace_use: If everyone is responsible for a check, often nobody is. Name the owner and the evidence of completion.
ethical_boundary: Accountability requires adequate authority, training and resources.

name: Treat small vulnerabilities before they compound
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VIII — vices and calamities
modern_rule: Weak signals, recurring deviations and unresolved friction deserve early attention before they become crises.
workplace_use: Repeated minor equipment alarms or procedural workarounds may signal a larger reliability or training issue.
ethical_boundary: Do not catastrophize; prioritize by evidence and consequence.

name: Plan for deterioration, stability and progress
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — deterioration, stagnation and progress
modern_rule: For major choices, examine best case, base case and downside case before committing.
workplace_use: Ask what you will do if the production plan works, partially works, or fails.
ethical_boundary: Scenario planning should guide preparedness, not paralysis.

name: Judge repeated consequences, not only immediate wins
classical_basis: Modern adaptation of Arthashastra's sustained emphasis on acquisition and preservation
modern_rule: Ask what happens if this decision pattern is repeated ten times.
workplace_use: A shortcut that saves ten minutes today may normalize a weak standard across the team.
ethical_boundary: Long-term strategy does not justify present unethical conduct.

name: Preserve credibility as strategic capital
classical_basis: Modern adaptation from Arthashastra's treatment of agreements, ministers and alliances
modern_rule: Your future influence depends heavily on whether people expect your words, standards and commitments to be reliable.
workplace_use: Be consistent between what you demand from others and what you tolerate from yourself.
ethical_boundary: Reputation management must not replace truth or accountability.

name: Leadership succeeds through the welfare of those governed
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book I — ruler's interest linked to subjects' welfare
modern_rule: Sustainable leadership improves the system for the people doing the work, not merely the leader's status.
workplace_use: Ask whether a decision improves safety, clarity, capability and fair conditions while meeting business needs.
ethical_boundary: Team welfare and organizational duty must be balanced; neither is a license to ignore the other.

name: Do not worship one tactic
classical_basis: Arthashastra, Book VII — six policies vary with conditions
modern_rule: The right strategy depends on relative strength, timing, information, stakes and alternatives.
workplace_use: A manager who only persuades becomes ineffective; one who only disciplines becomes feared. Choose based on conditions.
ethical_boundary: Adaptability does not mean abandoning principles.
